title: Why Koalas Eat 500g of Poison Leaves a Day 🐨
description:
Why do koalas only eat eucalyptus leaves when they're tough, low in nutrients and toxic to most animals? A koala's two-metre caecum is packed with millions of gut bacteria that break down the fibre, so koalas eat up to 500 grams of leaves a day and sleep up to 22 hours to save energy.

topic: Why don't koalas eat anything but eucalyptus?
script: Koalas eat poison leaves you'd never survive. So why only eucalyptus? Eucalyptus leaves are tough, low in nutrients, and toxic to most animals. So koalas get the trees to themselves. Their secret is inside. A koala's gut has a pouch called the caecum, about two metres long, packed with millions of bacteria. They break down the tough fibre, and help deal with the toxins. Even then, a koala absorbs only a quarter of it. So it eats up to five hundred grams of leaves a day, gets almost all its water from them, and saves energy by sleeping, up to twenty-two hours a day. And baby koalas? They eat a special mum poop called pap, to get those gut bacteria. So, would you eat poison leaves, if it meant twenty-two hours of sleep?
key_facts: Eucalyptus leaves are fibrous, low in nutrition and poisonous to most animals (Australian Koala Foundation; National Geographic)
The koala's caecum is about 200 cm long and holds millions of bacteria that break down the fibrous leaves (Australian Koala Foundation)
Koalas absorb only about 25% of the fibre they eat (Australian Koala Foundation)
Each koala eats about 200-500 g of leaves a day and gets most of its water from them (Australian Koala Foundation; National Geographic)
Koalas sleep 18 to 22 hours a day (Australian Koala Foundation; National Geographic)
Joeys feed on pap, a special form of the mother's droppings that passes on gut microbes (Discover Wildlife / AKF)
